_readme: LocalAI Studio model catalog — add, remove, or edit models here. Each entry maps to a model card in the Models tab. Fields: id (unique key), name, vendor, category (Ultra Small|Small|Medium|Large|Extra Large|Vision|Speech|Embeddings|Document AI|Image Generation), description, parameters, size_gb (download size), min_ram_gb, min_vram_gb (set 0 for CPU-only), context_length, ollama_tag (ollama pull tag — required for text models), comfyui_model (checkpoint filename — required for image generation models), comfyui_model_url (direct download URL for the checkpoint, optional), learn_more_url (optional exact external model page), backend (omit or 'ollama' for text models; 'comfyui' for image models; or a benchmark adapter backend such as transformers, onnxruntime, onnx-genai, openvino, sentence-transformers/onnx, faster-whisper/onnx), hf_repo/onnx_repo/ov_repo (HuggingFace repo or null), hf_revision (required for trust_remote_code utility models AND for any user_added entry — always a resolved 40-char commit SHA, never a branch name), onnx_subfolder (optional), tags (list of strings), chat_selectable (optional bool override for Chat page visibility), ollama_num_ctx (optional per-model Ollama chat context cap), ollama_keep_alive (optional Ollama keep_alive value such as '30m'), benchmark_skip_reason (optional reason to remove a known-bad model from pass/fail benchmark suites). Image Generation models may set supports_img2img=true and img2img_workflows (denoise_default/min/max) to enable reference-image generation via ComfyUI. Image Generation models MUST also include recommended_settings AND perf_profile blocks (validated at startup). Optional Add-from-Hugging-Face fields: user_added=true (marks an entry added via the Models > + Add from Hugging Face dialog), requires_review=true (surfaces a banner in the detail pane when the compatibility verdict was warn or the user overrode unsupported), source_url (the original pasted Hugging Face / Ollama URL), added_at (ISO 8601 UTC timestamp). Optional SKU compatibility is computed at runtime when a private SKU file is present. By default merge_builtins=true adds new built-in defaults on app updates; set merge_builtins=false for JSON-only behavior, or list IDs in disabled_builtin_ids to hide selected built-in defaults. Reload takes effect via Settings > Reload Catalog (no restart needed). Unknown fields are preserved on reload; keep curation notes in external reports rather than in the shipped catalog.

models.name: Qwen 2.5 0.5B
models.description: Alibaba's tiniest Qwen model. Surprisingly capable for its size. Good for quick tests on any hardware.

models.name: Llama 3.2 1B
models.description: Meta's compact 1B model. Strong reasoning for its size, runs well on CPU.

models.name: Llama 3.2 3B
models.description: Meta's 3B model with a massive 128K context window. Great for document analysis on modest hardware.

models.name: Phi-4 Mini 3.8B
models.description: Latest Phi Mini, improved on Phi-3.5 across benchmarks. Great coding and STEM performance.

models.name: Llama 3.2 Vision 11B
models.description: Meta's multimodal 11B model with image understanding. An older, heavier alternative to Gemma 3 for the Analyze → Prompt feature on the Image Generation page. Prefer Gemma 3 4B (Recommended) or Gemma 3 12B (Highest Accuracy) unless you specifically want this model.

models.name: Gemma 3 4B
models.description: Google's Gemma 3 4B multimodal model. Best balance of accuracy and speed for everyday image understanding and the Analyze → Prompt feature on the Image Generation page. Recommended default for vision tasks.
models.tradeoff_note: Best balance of accuracy and speed for most image tasks.

models.name: Gemma 3 12B
models.description: Google's Gemma 3 12B multimodal model. Highest accuracy and prompt fidelity for image understanding — slower than Gemma 3 4B but worth it when quality matters more than latency.
models.tradeoff_note: Highest measured accuracy; slower than Gemma 3 4B.

models.name: MiniCPM-V
models.description: OpenBMB's MiniCPM-V — efficient multimodal model with strong practical image understanding and good OCR / multilingual behavior at lower VRAM than 12B-class vision models.
models.tradeoff_note: Efficient multimodal model with good OCR and multilingual support.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1 32B Distill Q4
models.description: R1 reasoning at 32B scale, quantised to Q4. Near frontier-level reasoning performance. Requires ~20 GB VRAM (24 GB GPU).

models.name: SDXL 1.0 Base
models.description:
Stable Diffusion XL base model. Much higher quality than SD 1.5, especially for 1024×1024. Requires 8 GB VRAM (8 GB+ GPU).

Speed/quality: balanced reference SDXL at 1024². ~17–22 s on 24 GB VRAM. Best baseline for high-res output.
models.showcase_prompt: a majestic golden eagle in mid-flight soaring over snow-capped Alpine mountains at golden hour, cinematic lighting, sharp focus, photorealistic, 8k detail, magazine cover
models.tradeoff_note: Speed/quality: balanced reference SDXL at 1024². ~17–22 s on 24 GB VRAM. Best baseline for high-res output.

perf_profile.notes: Solid SDXL workhorse — runs almost anywhere with 8 GB+ VRAM.

models.name: Flux.1 Schnell Q4
models.description:
Flux.1 Schnell quantised to Q4. State-of-the-art image quality at high speed. Prompt following far exceeds SD/SDXL. Requires 8 GB VRAM (8 GB+ GPU).

Speed/quality: SPEED — 1–4 step distilled Flux Schnell, Q4 quant. ~6–15 s at 1024². Lower fidelity than Dev.
models.tradeoff_note: Speed/quality: SPEED — 1–4 step distilled Flux Schnell, Q4 quant. ~6–15 s at 1024². Lower fidelity than Dev.

perf_profile.notes: Fast Flux — near-Dev quality in 4 steps; outstanding speed/quality.

models.name: Flux.1 Dev Q4
models.description:
Flux.1 Dev quantised to Q4. Highest quality of the Flux family — slower than Schnell but more detailed outputs. Requires 10 GB VRAM (12 GB+ GPU).

Speed/quality: MEMORY — 4-bit Flux.1 Dev. Runs in ~10 GB VRAM with mild quality loss vs FP16. ~45–70 s.
models.showcase_prompt: A cozy bookshop interior at twilight, a calico cat sitting in the window with a wooden sign that reads "Open Late" hanging beside it, golden hour light spilling between bookshelves, photorealistic, shallow depth of field
models.tradeoff_note: Speed/quality: MEMORY — 4-bit Flux.1 Dev. Runs in ~10 GB VRAM with mild quality loss vs FP16. ~45–70 s.

perf_profile.notes: Best quality you can fit in 10 GB; Flux Dev quantized to Q4.

models.name: Flux.1 Dev FP16
models.description:
Flux.1 Dev at full FP16 precision. Maximum quality — the reference implementation. Needs ~24 GB VRAM (24 GB GPU only).

Speed/quality: QUALITY (slow + heavy) — full-precision Flux.1 Dev. ~60–90 s, requires ~24 GB VRAM. Best Flux output.
models.tradeoff_note: Speed/quality: QUALITY (slow + heavy) — full-precision Flux.1 Dev. ~60–90 s, requires ~24 GB VRAM. Best Flux output.

perf_profile.notes: Flagship Flux at full precision — needs 24 GB VRAM.

models.name: Juggernaut XL v9
models.description:
RunDiffusion's premier SDXL photorealism fine-tune. Exceptional skin texture, natural lighting, and photojournalistic quality at 1024×1024. Best SDXL model for executive demos. Runs on 8 GB VRAM.

Speed/quality: QUALITY — SDXL photoreal fine-tune. ~20–25 s. Top pick for cinematic realism.
models.tradeoff_note: Speed/quality: QUALITY — SDXL photoreal fine-tune. ~20–25 s. Top pick for cinematic realism.

perf_profile.notes: Top SDXL photoreal fine-tune — portraits, scenes, products.

models.name: Realistic Vision v6.0
models.description:
The definitive SD 1.5 photorealism fine-tune. Produces strikingly realistic portraits and scenes at 512–768 px. Fast generation, 4 GB VRAM, enormous LoRA compatibility. No VAE baked in — pair with vae-ft-mse-840000 for best color.

Speed/quality: balanced SD1.5 photoreal fine-tune. ~5–10 s on 24 GB VRAM. Best SD1.5 choice for portraits.
models.tradeoff_note: Speed/quality: balanced SD1.5 photoreal fine-tune. ~5–10 s on 24 GB VRAM. Best SD1.5 choice for portraits.

perf_profile.notes: Tiny SD 1.5 photoreal — runs anywhere; very fast iteration.

models.name: Z-Image Turbo
models.description:
Z-Image's distilled fast variant, repackaged by Comfy-Org for native ComfyUI use. Generates high-quality photorealistic images in just 8 steps using a Qwen 3 text encoder and Flux VAE — blazing fast with strong prompt adherence. 12 GB VRAM. Support files (~6 GB for Qwen encoder + VAE) are downloaded automatically.

Speed/quality: SPEED — distilled Z-Image. ~5–10 s, near-base quality.
models.tradeoff_note: Speed/quality: SPEED — distilled Z-Image. ~5–10 s, near-base quality.

models.name: SDXL Lightning
models.description:
ByteDance distilled SDXL — sharp photorealism in 8 steps via the full ComfyUI checkpoint. (SDXL Lightning, HF #14, ♥ 2,148)

Speed/quality: SPEED — 2/4/8-step SDXL distillation. ~3–8 s at 1024². Near-base quality with the right step count.
models.showcase_prompt: a Bengal tiger leaping through a wall of crystal-clear water droplets, hyper-detailed fur, slow-motion, dramatic side lighting, nature photography
models.tradeoff_note: Speed/quality: SPEED — 2/4/8-step SDXL distillation using the full ComfyUI checkpoint. ~3–8 s at 1024². Near-base quality with the right step count.

perf_profile.notes: 8-step Lightning UNet — keeps SDXL quality at distill speed.

models.name: playground v2.5 1024px aesthetic
models.description:
Playground v2.5 — SDXL-arch retrained from scratch for aesthetics. Top-tier color and contrast. (Stable Diffusion XL, HF #55, ♥ 763)

Speed/quality: QUALITY — SDXL-based aesthetic fine-tune. ~20–28 s. Excellent for stylized photo-art.
models.showcase_prompt: a hyperrealistic close-up of an iridescent beetle on a dewdrop-covered leaf, macro photography, soft morning light, shallow DOF, National Geographic style
models.tradeoff_note: Speed/quality: QUALITY — SDXL-based aesthetic fine-tune. ~20–28 s. Excellent for stylized photo-art.

perf_profile.notes: Aesthetic SDXL successor — CFG=3 by design; vibrant results.

models.name: Counterfeit V3.0
models.description:
Counterfeit V3.0 — last in the seminal SD 1.5 anime series. (Stable Diffusion 1.5, HF #74, ♥ 562)

Speed/quality: balanced SD1.5 anime/illustration merge. ~5–10 s.
models.showcase_prompt: masterpiece, best quality, beautiful anime girl with long flowing pink hair, sakura petals, traditional shrine background, kimono with intricate floral pattern, soft natural light
models.tradeoff_note: Speed/quality: balanced SD1.5 anime/illustration merge. ~5–10 s.

perf_profile.notes: Polished anime SD 1.5 v3 — clean lineart and color.

models.name: SDXL Low VRAM
models.description: Low-VRAM SDXL profile for small-GPU demonstrations using the SDXL Base checkpoint.
models.benchmark_skip_reason: SDXL Low VRAM benchmark path is covered by sdxl-base; the --lowvram cold-start on 24 GB SKUs is non-deterministic (ComfyUI subprocess exits during pytorch attention init).

perf_profile.notes: Solid SDXL workhorse — runs almost anywhere with 8 GB+ VRAM.
